LBR.note: LCERT is named as a council member and as the body a bill would fund and give duties, but the document states no creation by law, no incident handled and no designation.

facts.fact: The Liberian Senate passed the Cybercrime Act of 2025, described as a proposed Act, with amendments on 4 November 2025, after a joint committee report; the document does not say it was promulgated.

LBR.note: The Act is a cybercrime bill with a data-breach reporting section; it is not a general data protection law and states no standing for one.
Nothing stated on a data protection law in force, ratification, an authority or its practice.
ISO/IEC 27001 is named only in a proposed Act's standards clause; no membership, adoption or binding requirement is stated.

facts.fact: The Senate joint committee on Post and Telecommunications, Judiciary and Claims and Petition said its review of the draft Cybercrime Act was guided by a public hearing.

LBR.note: No national standards body or issued national standard is stated.
The bill only calls for Liberia to accede to the Malabo and Budapest Conventions and was benchmarked on ECOWAS and AU texts; no signature, ratification or giving effect is stated.
